meta.address: Plot No. F-01, Sector 6, Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201301
meta.frame: Local frame. Origin = ground level at the corner between the side elevation (B) and the front elevation (A); that corner is the left edge of the white corner pier in the photograph. +X runs along elevation A (left to right in the photo). +Y runs along elevation B away from the camera. A faces -Y, B faces -X. The exported model is re-centred on the footprint centre.
meta.facade_u_v: u is the distance along an elevation, v is the height above ground. Elevation A: u from the corner (x = u). Elevation B: u from its far end (left edge in the photo), so y = side_length_B - u.

confidence_scale.medium: measured from the reference photograph against a stated dimension
confidence_scale.low: estimated from the photograph without a reference dimension, or inferred where the photograph does not show it

developer.facts: Single tower of G+4 with dedicated basements; total leasable area 90,551 sq ft; plot size 2,940 sq m; Plot No. F-01, Sector 6, Noida.

autopilot_listing.facts: Configuration G+4 commercial tower; dedicated basement parking.

tenant_clovia.facts: Clovia Corporate Office, 4th Floor, Plot 1, F Block, Sector 6, Noida (explains the Clovia signage).

tenant_sprint.facts: Sprint F1 Skymark, 3rd Floor, Sky Mark Building, F1 Sector 6.

photo.description: Elevated three-quarter view (about roof height), portrait, roughly 830 x 900 px. Shows the front elevation nearly frontal and the side elevation receding to the left, with the road in the foreground.
photo.note: The photograph was supplied in the conversation and could not be saved as a file in the build environment, so it is not loaded as a pixel overlay. All photo measurements below were read from it by eye, in pixels, and converted with the scale noted on each block.

photo_scale_notes: Corner pier spans about 400 px from parapet to ground; the front about 361 px; side B about 309 px. Readings are by eye, good to about 10 px.

Height: G+4 at an assumed 4.1 m per floor plus a 2 m parapet = 22.5 m. Width and length were then set so the reference render reproduces the photo's width-to-height ratios (0.90 for the front, 0.77 for the side).

The far end of side B is about 0.7 times as tall in the image as the corner, which puts the camera about 88 m from the corner; 400 px for 22.5 m at 88 m is a 63 mm lens on a 36 mm sensor at this crop.
Yaw is about 32 degrees from the front's normal.
Positions along B were corrected for perspective: s = t / (1.43 - 0.43 t), where t is the image fraction from the far end and s the true fraction.
Roof lines fall and ground lines rise away from the corner in a ratio of about 1 to 2, which puts the camera about 15 m above the ground.

source.floor_to_floor: Photo: slab lines on the front glass are about 70 px apart against a 400 px pier, so 5 floors plus a 2 m parapet fill the height. 4.1 m is assumed as a normal office floor height; no source states it.
source.side_length_B: Same footprint: its 59.2 m long side less the 8 m podium in front of the street face. The features along this side were scaled from the photo fit (44.7 m) to 51 m.
source.front_width_A: Overture Maps footprint used by the earlier Skymark study (media/skymark-f1/site.json): 59.2 m by 33.9 m. The photo-fitted front (corner pier, glass, right pier) is stretched to fill the 33.5 m short side; there is no separate wing (the grey wing in an earlier render does not exist).

massing.hidden_sides: The rear and the far side are not visible in the photograph. They are closed with plain cladding massing only, tagged observed = false.

right_pier.source: photo: 38 px white pier at the right edge

parapet_band.source: photo: thick white band above the curtain wall

dark_recess.source: photo: darker glazed strip, about 45 px wide, between the corner pier and the lit glass; whether it is a recess or the return of a projecting glass box cannot be told from one view

end_pier.source: photo: white column at the far left end

top_ribbon.source: photo: strip of four wide openings with white piers between them, just under the parapet; its sill reads about 20 m up, which is above the middle of the 4th floor, so it may be partly a roof-level screen. Not resolved from one photo.

parapet_band.source: photo: side B's parapet reads about 1 m lower than the corner pier's top

angular_frame.source: photo: trapezoid frame; left edge vertical, right edge leaning toward the corner at the bottom. Corners read at (78,505) (215,510) (243,690) (78,640) px and converted with the perspective correction; expect 1 to 2 m of error along the facade and about 1 m in height

frame_top_band.source: photo: white ledge above the frame, reading as a projecting canopy from the far end to just past the frame

slanted_glazing.source: photo: blue-grey glazing between the frame's leaning edge and the white panel pier reads as an inclined plane following that edge

accent_strip.source: photo: full-height dark brown strip at the corner, between the white panel pier on B and the corner pier on A

ground_base.source: photo: dark base under the frame, partly hidden by trees and the boundary wall

upper_glazing.source: photo: dark band between the frame's top edge and the white ledge

corner_return_pier.source: photo: white panel grid, about 40 px wide and full height, between the glazing and the brown strip

annex.source: photo: two-storey block in front of the curtain wall, reaching about 40 px past the main block's right edge, with the second care / Clovia sign band on its parapet, pale glazing with white horizontal lines on the first floor and dark glazing on its left side. Its depth cannot be measured from a near-frontal view

entrance.name: SKYMARK F-1
entrance.source: Inferred. The podium's ground floor is glazed and the drive leads to it, but the doors are hidden behind the palms in the photograph. A recessed glass porch with two pairs of doors, a canopy, steps and a ramp is modelled; confirm on site.

mast.source: photo: lattice telecom mast above the left end of the roof; plan position estimated

site.source: developer: plot 2,940 sq m. Paving, wall, kerb, palms and trees are read from the photograph; their positions are approximate and the plot boundary is not surveyed.

gate.source: The photograph shows the boundary wall and the driveway kerbs (yellow and black) by the podium, but not the gate itself. A vehicle gate onto the drive, a pedestrian gate in line with the entrance and a guard cabin are what such a plot has; positions are assumed.

reference_camera.source: Solved by hand from the photograph (see meta.photo_scale_notes), then checked against test renders. No EXIF and no surveyed control points, so this is a visual match, not a calibrated camera.

pin.source: Centre of Skymark F-1's Overture Maps footprint, as used by the earlier Skymark study (media/skymark-f1/site.json and engine/atlases/skymark-f1.js on branch claude/determined-fermat-kowald)

map.note: Placed on the building's own footprint (Overture Maps, 59.2 m by 33.9 m), the one the earlier Skymark study matched to the client's Street View panorama. The street front, with the curtain wall and the podium, faces south-east (146 degrees); the long face with the angular frame faces south-west (236 degrees), along the road. The listing pin used before (28.593565, 77.318802) was about 270 m north, on open ground.

materials_note: Colours read from the photograph by eye. Glass is a tinted reflective surface (metallic 0.85 to 0.9, low roughness), so what it shows is mostly the sky and surroundings; two close variants of each glass and cladding are generated so panes and panels differ slightly.

interiors.source: Lit offices behind the glass so it reads like the photo, where ceilings and lights show through. A typical open office (light panels, desks with screens) is assumed; the real layouts are not known.
